name: GeneaCanvas GEDCOM Family Tree
author: Modern Solutions IT

sections.description:
GeneaCanvas GEDCOM Family Tree turns a GEDCOM file into an interactive family tree on your WordPress site. Build a family history website, share your genealogy research with relatives, or add a pedigree chart to any page, without retyping a single name.

Export a .ged file from your genealogy software, upload it to the Media Library, and paste one shortcode. Visitors can then explore your family tree on desktop, tablet and phone: zoom, drag, search for a person, and open a profile with dates, places and close relatives.

There is no limit on the number of people or family trees.

View the interactive demo | Learn about GeneaCanvas PRO

Family tree features in the free plugin

  • Forest of Clans: Start with an overview of every family line, then open the clan you want to explore.
  • All People view: See the whole family tree at once, with or without repeated people who connect several branches.
  • Pedigree chart: Pick any person and show a direct line of their ancestors, without collateral lines.
  • Descendants tree: Pick any person and show all of their children, grandchildren and later generations with their spouses, one card for each marriage.
  • Natural tree layout: An organic tree shape that keeps person cards from overlapping.
  • Dots for large trees: Show people as small dots to keep very large family trees fast and readable.
  • Search: Find a person by first name, surname, maiden or married name (when your GEDCOM file has it), year of birth or death, or place of birth or death, and jump straight to their place in the tree. Accents and letter case do not matter, so “lukasz” finds “Łukasz” and “sjogren” finds “Sjögren”. Several words narrow the results, for example “Nowak 1947”. Works with the keyboard, screen readers and on phones.
  • Person profiles: Click a person to see birth, christening, death and burial dates, places, spouses, children and other relatives, and move from one relative to the next.
  • Link to a person: Every opened profile gets its own address. Copy it with one click and send it to relatives: the link opens the tree directly on that person.
  • Relatives named properly: The profile lists a father, mother, brother, sister, husband, wife, son or daughter instead of generic labels, and groups all views of the person in one place.
  • Line highlighting: Point at a person to highlight their family line.
  • Zoom controls: Use the on-screen + and − buttons, the mouse, or touch gestures.
  • Full screen: One button opens the tree on the whole screen, on computers and phones. Press Escape or the same button to return to the page.
  • Minimap for large trees: When the tree does not fit on the screen, a small map of the whole tree shows where you are. Drag the frame or click the map to move around. On phones it waits behind a small button.
  • Generations at a glance: A slim bar on the left edge marks generations I, II, III… with the years of birth in each one. Click a mark to jump to that generation.
  • Breadcrumbs: A short path such as “Forest of clans › Clan Smith › John Smith (descendants tree)” shows where you are. Click any part of it to go back.
  • Made for phones: On small screens the tools move to a tidy menu with labelled groups and large buttons, the tree opens already framed, and a hint shows when there is more of the tree to drag into view.
  • Very large trees: Trees with tens of thousands of people stay smooth, because only the cards near the screen are drawn. Pages with big trees also open faster.
  • Sample tree and quick start: Try the plugin with one click on a small fictional family, then follow three short steps to your own tree. One more click creates a draft page with the tree.
  • Keyboard friendly: Move between people and buttons with Tab, open a profile with Enter and close it with Escape.
  • Dark theme: Besides the two light themes there is a dark one, “Dark Night”, with readable contrast (WCAG AA) on cards, panels and menus. Choose it in the shortcode generator, in the block or with theme="dark-night".
  • Calm motion on request: When “reduce motion” is turned on in the operating system or browser, the tree moves, zooms and opens panels without animations.
  • Family Tree block: Add the tree in the block editor with the “GeneaCanvas Family Tree” block and choose the tree and its options in the sidebar, without writing a shortcode.
  • Shortcode generator: Choose the starting view, layout, theme, expanded generations, height and titles, then copy a ready-made shortcode.
  • Reliable GEDCOM import: The character encoding is detected automatically (UTF-8, UTF-16, ANSEL, ANSI and ASCII), so accented letters display correctly. After each import you see how many people and families were read and whether any broken links were skipped.
  • Works with your theme: Use the block or the shortcode in the block editor, the shortcode in the classic editor, or any page builder that supports shortcodes.
  • Translations included: English, Polish, German, French, Spanish and Italian.

GeneaCanvas PRO for family history projects

Everything above stays free. GeneaCanvas PRO is a separate add-on for sites that need privacy, printing and richer family stories:

  • Privacy for living relatives: Dates, places and photos of living people are removed on the server and only appear after a family password is entered. You can also hide their first names.
  • Password for each shortcode: Protect the whole tree or only living people, separately on each page.
  • Hourglass view: Show the ancestors and descendants of a chosen person or marriage at the same time, and open it directly from a shortcode.
  • Fan chart of ancestors: A half or full circle with 3 to 8 generations in the colors of your tree, also as PDF or SVG.
  • Timelines: The life of one person event by event, or a whole family line decade by decade.
  • Animated family story and life story: Watch the family tree grow through the years, or follow one person from birth to grandchildren, with a year counter, captions and a summary. A slow projector show mode loops the story for family reunions.
  • Family map: Places of births, marriages and deaths on a map, with filters by family line, years and type of event.
  • Kinship calculator: Name the relationship between any two people and draw the line that connects them.
  • Print-ready posters in PDF and SVG: Export the tree as a framed poster with a title, in sizes up to A0 and 70 × 100 cm or on sheets to glue together. The download window suggests the size at which names stay readable.
  • Portrait photos: Add photos to people, with frames, shapes and sepia or black and white styles.
  • Theme editor: Change colors, fonts and card styles of seven ready-made themes, or create your own.
  • Full GEDCOM data: Show occupations, life events, biographical notes and sources in the person profile.
  • Document gallery: Attach scans of certificates and other documents to a person.
  • Family statistics: Most common names and places, lifespans, generations and births by century, in the tree or with a shortcode.
  • Family anniversaries: Show upcoming birthdays and wedding anniversaries in a widget or shortcode, with optional email reminders.
  • Suggestions from relatives: Let family members send corrections, photos, occupations, notes and events for you to approve.
  • Data check: A report of suspicious places in your GEDCOM file, such as impossible dates, unusual ages and possible duplicates, with a CSV download.
  • File version comparison: After you upload a new GEDCOM file, see who was added, removed or changed.
  • Clan filters: Show or hide clans by surname, ID or number of members for each shortcode.
  • Elementor widget: Place a tree in Elementor and set its options without writing a shortcode. PRO also adds its own options to the Family Tree block.
  • Priority support and automatic updates.

Works with popular genealogy software

GeneaCanvas reads standard GEDCOM 5.5 and 5.5.1 files, including exports from:

  • Gramps
  • RootsMagic
  • Family Tree Maker
  • MyHeritage
  • Ancestry
  • Legacy Family Tree
  • Ahnenblatt

Third-Party Libraries

This plugin includes D3.js 7.8.5 (ISC License) in minified form as js/d3.min.js. The source code is available at github.com/d3/d3.
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress admin go to Plugins > Add New, search for GeneaCanvas, then install and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to Trees (Canvas). While you have no trees yet, the screen shows three short steps with two buttons: Add tree and Load sample tree.
  3. Click Add tree, give your family tree a name and upload your .ged or .txt GEDCOM file. To try the plugin first, click Load sample tree instead: it adds a small fictional family as a draft tree.
  4. Publish the tree. The confirmation message shows the shortcode, for example [gcgft_tree id="12"], with a copy button and a Create a page with this tree button that opens a new draft page with the family tree block. Nothing is published until you publish the page yourself.
  5. Alternatively set the options in the Shortcode Generator panel and paste the shortcode into any page or post, or add the GeneaCanvas Family Tree block and choose the tree.

The list of trees shows the number of people, the shortcode with a copy button and the GEDCOM file with its upload date for every tree.
sections.faq:
How do I add a family tree to my WordPress site?

Export a GEDCOM file from your genealogy software, create a new tree under Trees (Canvas), upload the file, and paste the generated shortcode into a page. For example: [gcgft_tree id="123"]. In the block editor you can instead add the GeneaCanvas Family Tree block.

Can I try the plugin without my own GEDCOM file?

Yes. Click Load sample tree on the Trees (Canvas) screen or in the tree panel. The plugin adds a draft tree with a small fictional family (four generations, about 35 people, with christenings and burials) so you can see how the tree looks before you upload your own file. Clicking the button again does not add a second sample tree. You can delete the sample tree at any time.

Where does the sample tree come from?

The sample file assets/sample-family.ged ships with the plugin. It is plain GEDCOM data, not code: all people and places in it are invented. When you load it, the file is copied into your media library like any uploaded GEDCOM file. Nothing is downloaded from the internet.

How do I use the block?

In the block editor add the GeneaCanvas Family Tree block, choose the tree in the block sidebar and set the same options as in the shortcode generator. The editor shows a placeholder; the interactive tree appears on the published page.

How do I send someone a link to a particular person?

Open the person’s profile and click the link icon next to the close button. The copied address ends with #gcgft-person= and the person’s GEDCOM ID. Anyone who opens it sees the tree centered on that person, with the profile open.

My GEDCOM file shows strange characters instead of accented letters. What can I do?

GeneaCanvas detects the encoding from the file header and content, including UTF-8, UTF-16, ANSEL and ANSI (Windows-1252 and Windows-1250). The tree panel in the admin shows which encoding was used. If letters are still wrong, export the file again as UTF-8 from your genealogy software and upload it.

Which events are shown in the person profile?

Birth and death with dates and places, and also christening or baptism and burial or cremation when your GEDCOM file contains them. Occupations, notes, sources and other life events are part of GeneaCanvas PRO.

What is a GEDCOM file?

GEDCOM is the standard file format for exchanging family tree data. Nearly all genealogy programs and websites can export it, usually with an option such as “Export GEDCOM”. GeneaCanvas accepts .ged and .txt files.

Is there a limit on people or family trees in the free version?

No. You can import as many people and create as many family trees as your hosting can handle.

Does the family tree work on phones and tablets?

Yes. The tree supports touch gestures, and on smaller screens the tools move to a compact side menu. The full screen button is in that menu, and the minimap opens from a small button in the top corner of the tree.

How do I find my way around a very large tree?

Use Full screen to give the tree the whole screen. When the tree is bigger than the screen, the minimap in the corner shows the whole tree and a frame around the part you see: drag the frame or click anywhere on the map to move there (you can also hide it). The generation marks on the left edge tell you which generation you are looking at and its years of birth; click one to zoom to it. The path above the tree (breadcrumbs) takes you back to the clan or to the forest of clans in one click. Fit View always brings the whole clan back into view.

How big can my GEDCOM file be?

Trees with tens of thousands of people work: in very large views only the cards near the screen are drawn, so moving and zooming stay smooth also on phones. Reading the file needs server memory of roughly 25 times the file size (for example about 130 MB for a 5 MB file with 20,000 people). If the server limits are too low, the tree’s edit screen shows how much memory is needed and what to ask your hosting provider, instead of an error page.

Can I build a family tree by hand in WordPress?

No. GeneaCanvas displays data from a GEDCOM file. You edit your family tree in your genealogy software and upload the updated file, so that program stays the single source of your research.

How do I keep the data of living relatives private?

The free plugin shows everything in your GEDCOM file, so remove or anonymize living people before you export it. GeneaCanvas PRO can hide their data on the server behind a family password.

Can visitors download my GEDCOM file?

The GEDCOM file is stored in the WordPress media library like any other upload, so anyone who knows its exact address can download the whole file, including details that the tree itself hides. To make the address hard to guess, GeneaCanvas adds a random suffix to the name of every .ged file you upload (for example family-4k9x2m7q1z.ged). The safest approach is still to remove or anonymize living people in your genealogy program before you export the file.

How does the person search work?

Type at least two letters into the search box above the tree. You can search by first name, surname, other names from the GEDCOM file (for example a married or maiden name), a year of birth or death, or a place of birth or death. Letters with accents match plain letters, so you can type “zajac” to find “Zając”. Several words must all match, in any order: “Nowak 1947” or “Kraków Nowak”. Use the arrow keys and Enter, or tap a result, to go to that person. Living people protected by an extension can be found only by the name shown on their card, never by hidden dates or places.

How do I show the descendants of one person?

Open the person’s profile and click Show Descendants Tree (the button appears for people who have children in the GEDCOM file). The person and their spouse stand at the base, and each later generation grows above them. Back to Full Tree returns to the previous view. To start a page with this view, use for example [gcgft_tree id="123" view="descendants" person="I12"], where I12 is the person’s GEDCOM ID.

Which shortcode options are available?

With only the id, a tree starts as the Forest of Clans in the natural layout, without dots. The generator adds only the options you change:

  • view: unified-forest, giga-tree, giga-tree-duplicates, ancestors, descendants, or the GEDCOM ID of a clan founder
  • person: GEDCOM ID of the person for view="ancestors" or view="descendants", for example I12 (if the person does not exist, the tree starts as the Forest of Clans)
  • organic: yes or no
  • dot: yes or no
  • theme: modern-teal, classic-brown or dark-night
  • generations: expanded generations on startup, 1 to 15 (default 4)
  • clans: clans shown on the forest view, 1 to 100 (default 12)
  • height: for example 750px or 80vh
  • title and subtitle: header texts

Trees configured before version 1.2.0 keep their saved settings unless the shortcode sets a different value.

Can I display two different family trees on one page?

No. One family tree can be displayed per page. The same tree can be used on any number of pages, each with its own shortcode options.

Can I print my family tree or export it to PDF?

PDF and SVG export is available in GeneaCanvas PRO.
sections.changelog:
1.4

  • New: Descendants tree. Show all descendants of any person, with spouses, from the person profile or with view="descendants" and person in the shortcode. view="ancestors" with person starts a page with the pedigree chart.
  • New: Dark theme “Dark Night” with readable contrast (WCAG AA), available in the shortcode generator, in the block and as theme="dark-night".
  • New: “GeneaCanvas Family Tree” block for the block editor, with the same options as the shortcode generator.
  • New: Full screen mode, a minimap for large trees, a generation bar on the left edge and breadcrumbs above the tree.
  • New: Link to a person. Every opened profile has its own address with a copy button, and the link opens the tree on that person.
  • New: Sample tree with a fictional family, three first steps on the empty list of trees, and a “Create a page with this tree” button.
  • New: The list of trees shows the number of people, the shortcode with a copy button and the GEDCOM file with its upload date.
  • New: Christening or baptism and burial or cremation are read from the GEDCOM file and shown in the person profile.
  • New: Import summary in the tree panel: people, families, detected encoding and skipped broken references.
  • New: Public JavaScript API window.gcgft (events, methods and filters) for extensions and themes.
  • Enhancement: The natural layout grows upwards like a real tree, with a narrow trunk and a widening crown. Trees are up to 44% narrower, cards are lower and fuller, and lines never run under cards.
  • Enhancement: Search ignores accents and letter case, also searches years, places and other names from the file, accepts several words, highlights the match and works with the keyboard.
  • Enhancement: Very large trees. Only the cards near the screen are drawn, tree data loads almost twice as fast, and a GEDCOM file that is too big for the server limits shows a clear message with the memory needed instead of an error page.
  • Enhancement: GEDCOM import detects UTF-8, UTF-16, ANSEL, ANSI and ASCII, is faster and tolerates broken lines and references.
  • Enhancement: Mobile menu with labelled groups and two columns of buttons, one consistent icon set, touch targets of at least 44 px, and a tree that opens already framed.
  • Enhancement: The person profile names relatives by gender (brother, sister, husband, wife, son, daughter) and has a “Views of this person” section.
  • Enhancement: Keyboard support: Tab moves between people and buttons, Enter opens a profile, Escape closes it. Animations are skipped when “reduce motion” is turned on.
  • Enhancement: Numbers use the correct plural form and thousands separator in every language. Translations completed for Polish, German, French, Spanish, Italian and British English.
  • Fix: The ancestors and descendants views set in a shortcode are drawn again on phones and tablets.
  • Fix: A child listed in several families (for example adopted) is shown with the birth parents.
  • Fix: Names are read from the full name when the file has no separate given name and surname fields.
  • Fix: Living people are detected more reliably (christening year, death without a date, burial).
  • Fix: The clan title no longer covers cards, “Fit View” no longer puts cards under the toolbar, and cards no longer overlap in large expanded clans.
  • Fix: The collapse button always collapses the card under which it was clicked.
  • Fix: The tree title is no longer a second h1 heading on the page.
  • Security: Uploaded GEDCOM files get a random suffix in their file name, and the tree panel explains that the file itself can be downloaded by anyone who knows its address.
  • Security: For people protected by an extension, christening, burial and marriage dates and places are no longer sent to the page. Person IDs in the page are always escaped.
  • Tweak: Uninstalling the plugin removes only the tree cache. Trees, settings and GEDCOM files stay.

1.3

  • New: Shortcode generator. Starting view, layout, display mode, theme, generations, clan limit, height and titles are now shortcode options.
  • New: On-screen + and − zoom buttons.
  • New: The active tree ID is passed to the tree script and to extensions, with new hooks for tree rendering and clan lists.
  • Tweak: Shorter, clearer toolbar labels with descriptions on hover.
  • Tweak: Removed an unused landing page template, PRO-only styles and data, and debug logging.
  • Fix: Corrected many translations in German, French, Spanish, Italian and Polish.
  • Fix: Saving a tree no longer clears its cache when the GEDCOM file has not changed.
  • Fix: Families listed before individuals in a GEDCOM file no longer lose their relations.
  • Fix: A death record without a date now marks the person as deceased.
  • Fix: Plugin styles no longer affect the header and elements of the site theme.
  • Fix: GEDCOM dates are now translatable.
  • Fix: Clan names are escaped in the person profile.
  • Fix: Restored the icons shown before notes about multiple marriages and shared ancestors.
  • Security: Files with a .ged or .txt extension bypass the file type check only when they start with a GEDCOM header, and unpublished trees are visible only to users who can edit them.

1.2.4

  • Enhancement: Redesigned and streamlined top navigation bar controls — removed verbose “(Enabled)/(Disabled)” labels in favor of clean active toggle states (.is-active) matching theme hover styles.
  • Enhancement: Expanded responsive off-canvas menu breakpoint from 768px to 1024px to provide a clean, uncluttered layout with hamburger drawer navigation on tablets.
  • Enhancement: Fixed off-canvas button active and hover states so active features are distinct and clearly distinguishable on touchscreens.
  • Fix: Auto-close details sidebar when clicking ancestor/descendant relationships on tablets (<= 1024px) to ensure unblocked canvas framing.
  • Feature: Added GDPR / Privacy notice in wp-admin tree editor when living individuals are detected in uploaded GEDCOM files.

1.2.3

  • Fix: Resolved an issue where translations were ignored and the interface defaulted to English. Textdomain loading is now hooked early on init with proper relative path resolution.

1.2.2

  • Feature: Added a dedicated mobile off-canvas drawer menu (hamburger toggle) for toolbar controls on mobile devices (max-width: 768px).
  • Enhancement: Streamlined mobile viewport layout keeping only the search bar and family header visible for maximal tree canvas space on 100vh screens.
  • Fix: Relocated mobile off-canvas container to document body to eliminate clipping caused by overflow:hidden wrappers on various themes.
  • Fix: Fixed search navigation and person auto-focus when operating inside the Pedigree (ancestor) mode.
  • Fix: Raised search dropdown suggestions z-index to overlay clan title labels on mobile displays.
  • Fix: Auto-close individual details sidebar when navigating through blood line or spouse clan links to expose camera transitions.
  • Tweak: Replaced non-standard arrow glyphs with universal standard unicode arrows for consistent cross-device rendering.

1.2.1

  • Enhancement: Added full plugin translations for German (de_DE), French (fr_FR), Spanish (es_ES), and Italian (it_IT) to support a global user base.

1.2.0

  • Feature: Introduced the “Pedigree View” (Ancestors Mode). You can now select any person and generate a clean, direct-line ancestor chart upwards without collateral branches.
  • Feature: Added a “Return to full tree” reset button in the UI to seamlessly switch back to the complete canvas view.
  • Enhancement: Updated readme.txt tags to strictly comply with WordPress.org repository guidelines (limited to 5 tags).
  • Enhancement: Prepared core architecture to seamlessly integrate with new GeneaCanvas PRO features (Hourglass View, Interactive Maps, Kinship Calculator).

1.1.4

  • Fix: Fixed clan root detection and descendant tree building for multiple marriages — prevented mothers from hijacking husband clans and combining half-siblings under step-parents.
  • Enhancement: Added interactive background SVG tree artwork into the D3 canvas layer that zooms, pans, and dynamically adopts the active color theme.
  • Enhancement: Implemented dynamic bounding box calculation for the background tree — automatically resizes to fit small clans (1-2 generations) as well as massive Giga-Trees.
  • Fix: Bottom-anchored the background tree to ensure root ancestors and founder cards always sit naturally at the trunk and roots.
  • Fix: Fixed WordPress wp_localize_script boolean string-casting bug where startup settings for “Dot Mode” and “Organic (Beautiful) Tree” were ignored.
  • Fix: Resolved startup view bug where selecting “Giga-Tree” or specific clans defaulted back to the Forest view.
  • Fix: Added event protection against synthetic browser autofill and theme change events on the clan selector dropdown during page load.
  • Fix: Improved resetTreePerspective() camera framing with responsive scaling for mobile/tablet screens and support for Giga-Tree with duplicates.

1.1.3

  • Fix: Improved tree canvas rendering logic.
  • Tweak: Redesigned header layout into a structured two-row layout (clan title and statistics on top, toolbar controls below).
  • Fix: Removed unwanted theme margins between the clan title and subtitle.
  • Tweak: Removed bottom border line from the header for a cleaner, modern look.
  • Tweak: Improved responsiveness and alignment of the stats block and control buttons.

1.1.2

  • Enhancement: Redesigned mobile and tablet UX with an ultra-compact HUD and fixed bottom clan navigation bar.
  • Enhancement: Dynamic branch and line stroke highlighting now fully inherits active CSS theme colors.
  • Enhancement: Optimized D3.js spacing grid to ensure spouses and siblings never overlap in standard tree mode.
  • Enhancement: Integrated extensible JavaScript callback hooks for modular tree layout customizers.
  • Enhancement: Standardized all internal file operations using native WP_Filesystem and wp_delete_file APIs.
  • Fix: Expanded SVG foreignObject viewport bounds to eliminate rectangular clipping on glow highlight animations.
  • Fix: Added automated mobile sidebar drawer closing when navigating through relatives and search results.
  • Fix: Adjusted mobile z-index layering so full-width details drawers seamlessly overlay navigation controls.
  • Fix: Hardened security with comprehensive input unslashing, sanitization, and output escaping.
  • Fix: Unified all internal function prefixes and text domains to match WordPress.org standards.

1.1.1

  • Enhanced translation loading and text domain handling.
  • Expanded and improved documentation.
  • Performance optimizations for large GEDCOM datasets.

1.1.0

  • Initial public release on WordPress.org.

  • Fan chart of ancestors: A half or full circle with 3 to 8 generations in the colors of your tree, also as PDF or SVG.
  • Timelines: The life of one person event by event, or a whole family line decade by decade.
  • Animated family story and life story: Watch the family tree grow through the years, or follow one person from birth to grandchildren, with a year counter, captions and a summary. A slow projector show mode loops the story for family reunions.
  • Family map: Places of births, marriages and deaths on a map, with filters by family line, years and type of event.
  • Kinship calculator: Name the relationship between any two people and draw the line that connects them.
  • Print-ready posters in PDF and SVG: Export the tree as a framed poster with a title, in sizes up to A0 and 70 × 100 cm or on sheets to glue together. The download window suggests the size at which names stay readable.
  • Portrait photos: Add photos to people, with frames, shapes and sepia or black and white styles.
  • Theme editor: Change colors, fonts and card styles of seven ready-made themes, or create your own.
  • Full GEDCOM data: Show occupations, life events, biographical notes and sources in the person profile.
  • Document gallery: Attach scans of certificates and other documents to a person.
  • Family statistics: Most common names and places, lifespans, generations and births by century, in the tree or with a shortcode.
  • Family anniversaries: Show upcoming birthdays and wedding anniversaries in a widget or shortcode, with optional email reminders.
  • Suggestions from relatives: Let family members send corrections, photos, occupations, notes and events for you to approve.
  • Data check: A report of suspicious places in your GEDCOM file, such as impossible dates, unusual ages and possible duplicates, with a CSV download.
  • File version comparison: After you upload a new GEDCOM file, see who was added, removed or changed.
  • Clan filters: Show or hide clans by surname, ID or number of members for each shortcode.
  • Elementor widget: Place a tree in Elementor and set its options without writing a shortcode. PRO also adds its own options to the Family Tree block.
  • Priority support and automatic updates.

Works with popular genealogy software

GeneaCanvas reads standard GEDCOM 5.5 and 5.5.1 files, including exports from:

  • Gramps
  • RootsMagic
  • Family Tree Maker
  • MyHeritage
  • Ancestry
  • Legacy Family Tree
  • Ahnenblatt

Third-Party Libraries

This plugin includes D3.js 7.8.5 (ISC License) in minified form as js/d3.min.js. The source code is available at github.com/d3/d3.
